subject: Response-time cascade on Hosted API — immediate mitigation and update
messages:
From: Samira Qureshi <samira@fintechcorp.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fintechcorp.com
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 regression affecting nightly batch - urgent

Markus,

We're seeing a severe regression in response times across the Hosted API starting around 04:00 UTC this morning. p95 has jumped from ~480ms to ~2.4s and p99 from ~1.2s to ~6.8s. Concurrently, our error rate (5xx) increased from 0.2% to ~3.7% during the 04:00-06:00 window. This is impacting our nightly reconciliation and causing timeouts on downstream systems.

We run a steady stream of multi-turn generation requests (avg tokens ~1.1k) and saw a backlog of inflight requests queueing up; retries compounded the pile-up. Attached is our p95 chart and a sample request payload.

Can you triage and let us know immediate mitigation steps? Our SREs are available for a bridge.

Attachments: p95_graph.png (image/png), request-sample.json (application/json)

Thanks,
Samira Qureshi
Sr. Platform Engineer
FinTechCorp

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 regression affecting nightly batch - urgent

Hi Samira — thanks for the alert and the attachments. We're pulling the on-call SREs into a triage now.

Quick notes and immediate asks:
- We're aware of a config rollout last night that adjusted batching heuristics for high-token requests; that could be related.
- Can you confirm the percent of requests >1024 tokens during the spike window?
- We'll propose an immediate mitigation: (a) reduce batching window to 10ms for default route, (b) enable burst concurrency for your account, and (c) temporarily fall back to the legacy batching profile.

I'm looping in Monica (account lead) and Marissa (SRE) to get an operational plan and ETA. We'll keep this thread as the single source of truth.

Attachment: initial-analysis-checklist.txt

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Samira Qureshi <samira@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 regression affecting nightly batch - urgent

On Thu, Apr 18, 2028 at 08:52 AM Samira Qureshi <samira@fintechcorp.com> wrote:
> Markus,
> We're seeing a severe regression in response times...

Thanks Samira — reproducing your spike now in our telemetry. Initial findings:
- Root cause pointer: recent batching heuristic change (rolled at 23:40 local last night) increased the batching window for long requests when concurrency is low. That change unexpectedly lets large requests accumulate in a single batch, causing head-of-line blocking when one request has a long generation path.
- Evidence: queue depth for your account's route increased from median 4 -> 68 during the window; avg batch size jumped from 2 -> 17.
- We also saw a subtle interaction with the KV-cache warmup for long context lengths which extended tail latency for the earliest tokens.

Immediate mitigation plan (I can apply on approval):
1) Roll the batching window back to the pre-rollout value for your account and the default route (reduces head-of-line).
2) Lower max batch window to 10ms and cap batch size to 8 for requests >1024 tokens.
3) Temporarily enable your account's dedicated burst capacity (non-intrusive toggle) to absorb current backlog.
4) If needed, route a percentage (5-10%) of your traffic to a smaller-sequence-tailored model to avoid KV warmup penalty.

I've prepared a quick script to apply (takes ~3min) and a rollback command. If you approve, I'll push the mitigation and monitor p95/p99 in real-time.

Attachment: request-sample.json

—Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@fintechcorp.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 regression affecting nightly batch - urgent

Samira — apologies for the disruption. We're prioritizing this and I've escalated to CS leadership.

Marissa — please proceed with steps 1-3 immediately; Samira, we'll confirm before switching traffic to a model fallback (step 4).

Samira, I'll be on the bridge and will coordinate communications back to your ops team. Expect an initial mitigation live update within 15 minutes of this note and a short postmortem within 48 hours. I'll also loop in Marcus Lin for an exec-level brief if the issue persists beyond containment.

Thanks for the quick heads-up.

—Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@fintechcorp.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 regression affecting nightly batch - urgent

Update: containment complete.

Timeline recap:
- 09:20: rolled batching window to pre-rollout values for fintechcorp route; capped batch size for long requests.
- 09:25: enabled burst concurrency for FinTechCorp (temporary).
- 09:40: p95 returned to ~520ms; p99 trending down to ~1.3s. Error rate dropped under 0.5% by 10:05.

Root cause (summary): an opt-in heuristic intended to improve throughput for short-sequence workloads caused large-token requests to group into oversized batches; that produced head-of-line blocking and KV-warmup tail amplification for some requests.

Next steps:
- Permanent fix: revert heuristic and ship a refined batching policy with token-aware thresholds (ETA: 3 business days).
- Offer: applying a one-time usage credit for the impacted window; Monica will propose the credit amount.
- Postmortem: Marissa will publish a write-up with telemetry and pruned artifacts.

Samira — apologies again. We know this impacted critical jobs and will prioritize preventing regression. If you'd like an exec call, Marcus and I are available.

—Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
